owner: Council (system integration); co-sign HW-02 AI Core, HW-03 SRAM/TMA, HW-04 MC, HW-07 Comm Core, package / power
scope: The joint question L3 leaves open: each domain search (compute, sram, mc, comm, physical) chose its winner with every other domain held at the published point, so the five winners were never replayed together. integration/detailed/coupling_search.js composes them into one design point, replays it, and replays a small grid around it on three fixed couplings. The candidate set goes to out/detailed/coupling_candidates.json, the best joint point to out/detailed/coupling_design.json; design.coupling lands the chosen one as out/coupling/joint_point.json, the single global design point L4 and L5 read.
evidence: UNVERIFIED: drafted by an agent from the domain design spaces and doc 23 section 4, not by a domain owner. Every grid value is an option of the owning domain's own design space or of integration/detailed/die_area_reallocation.js MOVES; nothing here invents a hardware value. The replay is the K3 detailed model (MODEL); the comm core area is added as its own term because A.physical() does not size it, and its power is not modelled.

requirements.modelsReason: the joint replay is the detailed K3 TP32 model; the compute winner's kernel check still covers every model its own space requires (matrix_vector_design_space.json requirements.models)
requirements.contractReason: coupling owns no entry: it is the one step that has to hold all five at once, because it is the first place the five winners meet. B-SERIAL-CMP is tested through the contract target it was derived from (no searched dimension produces a computeScale), B-TAU on the slowest collective of the comm winner's control path at this point, the others on their own quantity
requirements.winnersReason: the composition reads each domain's design artifact (the hardware values it chose) and checks it against the candidate set it came from; a landed winner that names another option than the search winner stops the run instead of being silently replaced
requirements.tauPolicy: every row replays at tau = B-TAU max. tau is not a degree of freedom here: the contract allows any collective up to that ceiling, and a row that assumed a smaller one would be claiming slack the comm winner has not been asked to give. tauOverlapCompute rows carry a tau sweep and the slack of the slowest collective as a sensitivity

sramDepthMc.question: can MC bandwidth be traded for shared SRAM and prefetch depth (doc 23 section 4: SRAM capacity x prefetch depth x MC bandwidth)?
sramDepthMc.evidence: sharedMiB: sram_design_space.json options; depth: A.SPACE.depth (the prefetch depth the sram search left to coupling); mcGBs: memory_design_space.json options around the winner. Rows below B-SRAM-CAP or B-MEM-BW are replayed anyway and kept as rejected combinations with the clause named: they are the numbers an L1-b re-split would need

tauOverlapCompute.question: can collective time be hidden under compute (doc 23 section 4: tau x commOverlap x compute)?
tauOverlapCompute.evidence: vectorLanes: matrix_vector_design_space.json options around the compute winner (640 is below its binding kernel and stays as the rejected neighbour); commOverlap: the tuned model's O.OPT switch; tau: see requirements.tauPolicy

areaReallocation.question: is there a better use of the die area the domain winners left, moving it between SRAM, the matrix and Reduce/TMA/RDMA (doc 23 section 4, reusing die_area_reallocation.js)?
areaReallocation.moves: from the composed point: every single one-step move of every field, and every pair of one step down in one group with one step up in another. The steps are die_area_reallocation.js MOVES with the composed value inserted when the list does not carry it
areaReallocation.evidence: the step lists are die_area_reallocation.js MOVES (the same grid the area exploration climbs); the groups are doc 23's three area owners

constraints: every contract entry holds at the row: B-SRAM-CAP on sharedMiB, B-MEM-BW on mcGBs, B-TAU on the slowest collective (protocol + the comm winner's control path), B-SERIAL-CMP through the contract target, B-AREA on die area (shared-port charge, option overheads and the comm core included) and its die / card power limits
the K3 detailed replay at the row is feasible and reaches the contract target
every required H-core kernel of the compute winner still hides its vector work at the row's lanes and matrix shape
the package fits: dies x die area + cubes x cube area within the placement window less the physical winner's reserve, and the PHY shoreline within the die edge budget
objective: on the Pareto set of (TPS/usr up, die area down, card power down)
least die area, then least card power
